subject: Micronesia
note: Cited to pinned Wikipedia revisions (trusted_secondary): Mariana Trench and Challenger Deep, using the maximum known depth the Mariana Trench page headlines, 10,935 ± 6 m (the 2021 study named on the Challenger Deep page), and not the other measurements (10,903 to 11,009 m GEBCO range, 10,920 ± 9 m in 2011). Guam and Fais Island points come from their pinned pages. The profile is computed from NOAA ETOPO 2022 (1 arc-minute grid, about 1.8 km cells, public domain) along a straight line from Guam through the Challenger Deep to Fais Island; 626 km, lowest -10,466 m. The grid smooths the narrow slot, so this is the model's height along the line, not a surveyed section, and its low is not the Challenger Deep's depth. The panel prints the vertical stretch. The map draws no maritime limits.

claims.text: The Mariana Trench is the deepest oceanic trench on Earth, in the western Pacific Ocean, about 200 kilometers (124 mi) east of the Mariana Islands.
The maximum known depth is 10,935 ± 6 meters at the southern end of a small slot-shaped valley in its floor known as the Challenger Deep.
The trench is crescent-shaped and measures about 2,550 km in length and 69 km in width.
The deepest point of the trench is more than 2 km farther from sea level than the peak of Mount Everest.
At the bottom of the trench the water column exerts a pressure of 111 MPa, approximately 1,100 times the standard atmospheric pressure at sea level.
The closest land to the Challenger Deep is Fais Island, 287 km southwest, and Guam, 304 km to the northeast.
A 2021 study revised the depth of the Challenger Deep to 10,935 ± 6 m at a 95% confidence level.
A straight line of 626 km from Guam through the Challenger Deep to Fais Island (computed from NOAA ETOPO 2022).
Along that line the model's height falls to -10,466 m (computed from NOAA ETOPO 2022; 1.8 km cells smooth the narrow deep, which the page puts at 10,935 m).
